verdict.rationale: Phaser documents a first-party MCP server for Phaser Editor with over 40 specialised tools, and a Phaser Game Agent MCP server that coding agents connect to and call tools on. The editor page also describes scene-level operations such as creating particle emitters, reorganising layers and renaming objects, so the core of agent-driven scene editing is directly supported. missing for 10: a documented tool reference covering scene/node creation and property editing, any evidence of agent-triggered builds or exports, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can drive the editor and project programmatically — create scenes and nodes, edit properties, trigger builds — through a documented scriptable interface

citations.quote: For power users, the MCP Server goes deeper. It implements over 40 specialised tools and integrates directly with Claude Desktop, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and other MCP-compatible tools.
Build games from inside the editor you already use with the Phaser Game Agent MCP server.
You describe what you want in plain language and your agent calls the tools for you.
Create a particle emitter, reorganise a scene into layers, rename a bunch of objects — it handles it without switching tools.
